changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6310-designer-formula-key-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `designer.field.formula` (`'Formula (CEL)'`) in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, a different and live key belonging to metadata-admin's `ObjectFieldInspector` — the surface that still authors formula expressions.

### `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `table.noRows` (`'No rows to display'`) and `engine.form.noRows` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, read at `widgets.tsx`) — two different, same-named keys in different namespaces. Nor the comments in `WidgetEmptyState.tsx`, `DatasetWidget.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and `PivotTable.tsx` that record WHY three widgets with three strings became one shared empty state; the packs' own comment keeps that rationale and now names the retirement instead of a row that is gone.

### `.changeset/8632-malformed-picklist-option-loud.md`

- names `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Two new strings land in the designer's own `en` / `zh` tables — the metadata-admin console owns its strings in `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` and is deliberately outside the ten locale packs (`packages/i18n/README.md`, "Scope — the `engine.*` carve-out").

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `00715f5ba` (merge-base with origin/main): 9 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1418 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1998 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36100119337)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f18f4257fb69936792d7219ec4475f83a7b68186`

### ① Derived judgments

All line numbers are at the head `f18f425`, read with `git show refs/review/pr-10509:PATH`; the base is the merge-base `8c929e6`. The spec is the installed `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` (lockfile resolution at the head; `src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts` and `dist/automation/index.mjs`), probed with Node, not read from the report.

1. **`{token}` strings round-trip byte-identically, both shapes.** `FlowKeyValueField.tsx:59-64` (`toRaw` hands a string back as itself), `:67-85` (`parseValue` returns the untrimmed `raw` when brace-wrapped text is not JSON, so `{record.first} {record.last}` and `{amount}` survive), `:126-128` (`rowValue`: a text row goes through `parseValue` only), `:112-123` (`toRows` never gives a string row a `mode`), `:222-230` (`promoteEnvelopeText` promotes only text whose parse is an editable envelope, never a `{token}` string). Map and array pinned at `FlowKeyValueField.shape.test.ts:64-73`, the DOM commit at `FlowKeyValueField.valueEnvelope.test.tsx:70-74`. The pre-existing smart-parse re-typing (`'30'` to `30`, whitespace-only to `''`, `null` to `''`) is unchanged from the base and does not touch a `{token}` string. Judgment: holds.

2. **The stored envelope is exactly the spec's shape; nothing re-declared.** `flow-value-envelope.ts:51` reads the dialect off `AssignmentExpressionValueSchema.shape.dialect.value` (probe on 17.4.0: `"cel"`); `:100-108` writes `{ dialect: VALUE_DIALECT, source }` or patches a prior envelope's `source` (keeps `meta`, drops `ast`, hands an unedited one back by identity); `:113-116` the refusal is `AssignmentValueSchema.safeParse` issues verbatim (probe: every malformed case's message leads with `ASSIGNMENT_VALUE_ENVELOPE_REFUSAL`); `:70-73` the slot is read off `FLOW_NODE_EXPRESSION_PATHS` (probe: the value-role entries are exactly `assignment` / `assignments.*`); `:87-93` uses the spec's `isExpressionEnvelopeShaped`. The one local predicate, `isEditableValueEnvelope`, is a UI editability rule narrower than the spec recognizer (dialect `cel` plus a string `source`); a value the spec calls envelope-shaped but this rule rejects stays JSON text in the cell and is refused by the spec schema, never rewritten. `ValueEnvelope` is a `Pick` of the spec's own type. Judgment: holds.

3. **A malformed envelope surfaces the spec's refusal inline and is not silently stored as something else.** `FlowKeyValueField.tsx:316` computes the refusal per row from `rowValue(row)` through the spec; `:373-380` renders each message under `role="alert"`. A stored malformed envelope is read as text JSON (`:118-121`), and `parseValue` (`:77-83`) writes it back as the object, never a string (`shape.test.ts:97-103`). A blank expression writes `{ dialect: 'cel', source: '' }` and is refused inline (`shape.test.ts:104-108`; `valueEnvelope.test.tsx:84-95`, `template` dialect and blank source). The draft holds the value with the refusal visible, which is the triage's acceptable state (the bad case was an editor that stores a malformed envelope with no error). Judgment: holds.

4. **The affordance is offered only on the spec's value-role map.** `FlowNodeConfigField.tsx:146-151` passes `valueEnvelope` only when `isValueEnvelopeSlot(context?.node?.type, field.path)`; `flow-value-envelope.ts:64-70` requires a `['config', KEY]` path and a ledger entry with that node type, role `value` and path `KEY.*`. The production caller passes the node (`FlowNodeInspector.tsx:454`, `context={{ draft, node }}`), and `FlowNodeConfigField.tsx:131` is the only non-test caller of `FlowKeyValueField`. The pin at `flow-value-envelope.test.ts:31-50` enumerates every hand-table keyValue field (15 of them: `fields`, `filter`, `headers`, `inputs`, `variables`, `defaults`, `input`, `connectorConfig.input`, `params`, `timeRelative.filter`, and `assignments`) and requires the offered set to be exactly `assignment:config.assignments`; the DOM control on `create_record` `fields` is `valueEnvelope.test.tsx:64-66`. Descriptor-derived keyValue fields go through the same predicate and cannot match. Judgment: holds.

5. **Legacy array shape.** `FlowKeyValueField.tsx:114` (the array never reads envelopes), `:136-138` (`writesArrayShape`: array while no row is an expression), `:153-158` (else the canonical map), `:300` (no refusal while the array is written, since an envelope-shaped object is a literal there), `:305-309` (the spec's `ASSIGNMENT_ARRAY_FORM_PRESCRIPTION` shown as a note). This is consistent with the spec's declaration: the ledger comment says an envelope-shaped object in the array is a literal, the prescription says the map is the only shape that accepts an envelope, and `AssignmentConfigSchema` refuses the array. The PR never writes an envelope where the spec reads a literal, and converts only on the author's explicit toggle, to the shape the spec prescribes. Data: every kept `(variable, value)` pair carries across (`shape.test.ts:90-94`; DOM `valueEnvelope.test.tsx:97-105`); the base editor already normalized `name`/`key` aliases to `variable` and dropped any other entry key on every write, so the head loses nothing the base kept. Edge cases that change meaning: (a) an envelope-shaped literal already inside a legacy array becomes an evaluated expression once another row's toggle writes the map, same bytes, different meaning; the row visibly flips to expression mode after the flush (`:274`) and a malformed one is then refused inline, but the note is the spec's general prescription and no prose tells the author that this specific value's meaning changed; (b) integer-like variable names lose the array's order in a JS object map, theoretical; (c) pre-existing in both shapes and unchanged: `null` to `''` and `'30'` to `30` on any write. Judgment: sound; (a) is the one silent-meaning edge and it is a corner of an unused shape (see ③).

6. **Published surfaces.** `packages/app-shell/package.json` exports stay `.` and `./styles.css`; `src/index.ts` does not reach the inspectors; no api-surface file changed. New module-level exports `toRows`, `switchRowMode` (`FlowKeyValueField.tsx:112`, `:166`) and the `flow-value-envelope.ts` symbols are internal to app-shell. README (`packages/app-shell/README.md:523-529`) and guide (`content/docs/guide/flow-designer.md:124-142`) prose is judged in ②. Judgment: no published surface moves.

7. **Card coverage.** Asked and delivered: a per-value text / expression choice; the envelope stored; the spec refusal inline; the stdlib reachable (`joinNonEmpty(...)` pinned unrefused and unflagged, `valueEnvelope.test.tsx:60-63`, `flow-value-envelope.test.ts:81`); `{token}` byte-identical; both storage paths through one `rowValue`; pins beside `FlowKeyValueField.shape.test.ts`; one changeset; locale keys in both designer tables (`i18n.ts:409-410`, `:2377-2378`; the file has only `EN` and `ZH` engine tables, so parity is complete). Done but not asked: the array-form note; `mono` on expression rows; the two helper exports for pins; the behaviour-preserving `removeRow` refactor (`:290-292`); the README and guide paragraphs. Nothing asked is missing.

### ② Semver level

`'@object-ui/app-shell': minor` is correct: a new authoring feature; AGENTS.md 版本号策略 says objectui never declares `major` (even its own breaking changes are `minor`) and app-shell sits in the 40-package fixed group of `.changeset/config.json`. CI's `Changeset Bump Policy` and `Changeset Fixed Group Check` are green at the head.

Changeset prose, sentence by sentence: the title sentence, true. "now has a per-value toggle, Write as a CEL expression", true (`FlowKeyValueField.tsx:345-358`, label `i18n.ts:409`). "Off, the value is text: a `{token}` string is stored exactly as typed, and numbers, booleans and JSON literals are smart-parsed as before", true (item 1). "On, the value is stored as the CEL value envelope the spec declares for this slot, `{ dialect: 'cel', source }`, so the CEL stdlib can be authored from the designer", true (item 2; the runtime claim is the spec's own description). The JSON example, true to what the editor writes. "The editor reads which maps take an envelope from the spec's expression ledger; every other key/value map is unchanged", true (item 4). "A malformed envelope (no source, a blank one, a non-cel dialect) shows the spec's `AssignmentValueSchema` refusal beside the cell, and is kept as the object it is rather than turned into a string", true at the installed 17.4.0 (item 3; see the floor flag in ③). "A node still using the legacy array shows the spec's prescription for it. Switching one of its values to an expression writes the canonical map, the only shape the spec reads an envelope in; the other values move across unchanged", true as data (item 5, with the pre-existing smart-parse re-typing applying as it always did).

README `:523-529`: "On a map the spec's expression ledger declares value-role (today the assignment node's Assignments), each value also has a Write as a CEL expression toggle", true. "off, a `{token}` string is stored exactly as typed", true. "on, the value is stored as the CEL value envelope `{ dialect: 'cel', source }`", true. "a malformed envelope shows the spec's `AssignmentValueSchema` refusal inline", true for the map, which is the sentence's scope. It does not mention that the legacy array also shows the toggle; incomplete, not false.

Guide `:124-142`: "sets one variable per row. Each value is either text or a CEL expression, chosen with the row's toggle", true. "The node's config then reads" plus the JSON fence, true. "Text is `{token}` interpolation and is stored exactly as typed", true. "An expression is stored as the envelope and evaluated by the expression engine, so the CEL stdlib is available", true as the spec's declared runtime contract; note that the designer's own simulate panel (`previews/simulator/flow-simulator.ts:324-346`, `interpolateValue` at `:355` returns a non-string unchanged) passes the envelope object through as a literal, which the PR itself names as an out-of-scope finding. "A malformed envelope shows the spec's refusal under the cell", true. "The toggle appears only on maps whose values the spec declares may be an expression; other key/value editors have none", true (item 4).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR body flags.** Surface: `FlowNodeConfigField.tsx` (the sole caller, a one-prop wire in the same cleared directory), the README bullet and the guide paragraph were outside the claim's file list; disclosed in the body, no other claim names the directory, and the additions are the minimum wire plus repo-required docs. Acceptable; the seat's call, since the claim said stop on breach. Commit trailers: the four commits carry a model name in `Co-Authored-By`, against the dispatch contract; a squash merge replaces them, so this is a process flag only.
